correctness.rationale: For \(\rho=0\), setting \(a=r+1\) and \(b=g-D+r\) gives \(ab=g\) and the classical Castelnuovo count \(N_g(a,b)=g!\prod_{i=0}^{a-1} i!/(b+i)!\). Its denominator is the hook product of the \(a\times b\) rectangle. The package's cumulative hook-count formula is correct in each threshold range. For \(1\le a<c\le e<b\) with \(ab=ce\), the more balanced rectangle has at least as many hooks below every threshold and strictly more at some threshold, so after sorting its hooks coordinatewise they are no larger and at least one is smaller. Hence its hook product is strictly smaller and its tableau/Castelnuovo count is strictly larger. Iterating over divisor pairs proves the closest-divisor maximizer, while transposition gives exactly the Serre-dual tie. The finite genus-300 checker is corroborative only and is not needed for the quantified proof.
residual_risks: The main proof depends on the stated cumulative-hook dominance; the finite checker does not certify the infinite theorem, but the symbolic threshold argument does.

originality.rationale: The classical and modern Brill–Noether sources inspected this round give the pointwise zero-dimensional count for a fixed numerical type, not a fixed-genus ordering across all divisor rectangles. Resultary returned the assigned record as the only exact fixed-genus balancing hit, and targeted searches under rectangular standard-tableau, hook-product, fixed-area, balance, and closest-divisor formulations did not locate an earlier theorem. The balancing lemma is not mechanically implied by merely knowing the hook-length formula: it supplies a new strict comparison across distinct factor shapes. Best-of-knowledge originality therefore passes, with an explicit risk that an equivalent rectangle-monotonicity theorem may exist under older algebraic-combinatorics terminology.
residual_risks: An older theorem on monotonicity of rectangular standard Young-tableau counts at fixed area may exist under terminology not surfaced by the searches.
